CHAPTER IV
ADVERSE ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACTS WHICH CANNOT BE AVOIDED
A. Review of key adverse environmental impacts resulting from the recommended action: 
   Construction within redevelpment area and the resulting dust, noise, increased traffic, and other associated construction aspects.
2. Relocation of residents within redevelopment areas of the project.
3. The largest adverse environmental impact with result from the Downtown Expressway. Increased numbers of automobiles and trucks moving through the northern edge of the project area will result in higher concentrations of air and noise pollution. Other potential adverse conditions could result from expressway run-off and lighting. In all fairness to the Randolph Project, it must be clearly understood that these impacts on the community will be greater if the proposed renewal plan is not carried out.
B. Adverse environmental impacts of the project which could be avoided: 
1. If the alternatives of project relocation or "no action" were adopted no relocation or new construction would take place. However, the adverse environment already permeates the project as a result of existing conditions.
C. Adverse environmental impacts of the project which could not be avoided by any alternative: 
1. Regardless of the project, project alternatives, or HUD decisions, the Downtown Expressway will be constructed. The fate of the Randolph Plan will not affect the proposed Downtown Expressway.
D. Adverse environmental impacts of alternatives which were avoided by choosing the recommended action: 
1. A continuing deterioration of housing conditions within the project area.
2. A continuation of abandoned properties, overgrown lots, littered dirt alleys, overcrowded streets, streets without walkways, and insufficient usable open space.
3. A continuation of unsafe and unsanitary living conditions.
